source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Genesis 37–41.

key_decisions.decision: Prevents the common error of naming Judah’s unnamed wife Shua and states the sexual idiom plainly.
Names Tamar’s widowhood and explains the kinship duty without implying ordinary marriage consent.
States the repeated sexual exploitation and deliberate refusal of family duty without euphemism or misidentifying the offense.
Separates Judah’s stated promise from his concealed fear and preserves Tamar’s constrained position.
Preserves Tamar’s deliberate response to Judah’s broken obligation without moralizing it.
States the proposed transaction clearly while preserving Judah’s ignorance.
Renders qedeshah distinctly while leaving its precise institutional meaning to a note.
Preserves the accusation and Judah’s severe command without softening the threatened violence.
Restores Tamar as named speaker and preserves the recognition demand echoing Genesis 37:32.
Renders relative righteousness as being more in the right and makes the sexual euphemism clear.
Preserves the awkward breach wordplay underlying Perez rather than smoothing it away.
